facts.content: Diffuse blanching pruritic rash likely viral or related to insect bites needs examination and testing.
facts.source_text: 2) Rash, diffuse, blanching, pruritic. - Summary: Diffuse red itchy rash that reportedly blanches on pressure; likely viral or related to recent insect bites/immune reaction; needs examination and possible testing

facts.content: Telemedicine visit deemed insufficient; urgent in-person assessment required.
facts.source_text: 3) Need for in-person clinical assessment and possible urgent investigations/admission.

facts.content: Arrange urgent in-person examination at a Babylon hub today.
facts.source_text: Urgent in-person examination at a Babylon hub as soon as possible today (preferably within a few hours).

facts.content: If hub appointment unavailable or symptoms worsen, patient should go to the emergency department immediately.
facts.source_text: If hub appointment unavailable or symptoms worsen, go to emergency department (ED) immediately.

facts.content: Planned focused physical exam will include neurological and skin examinations and vital signs.
facts.source_text: Perform focused physical exam including full neurological exam (meningeal signs), skin examination (document blanching vs non-blanching), and vital signs including measured temperature, heart rate, blood pressure, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation.

facts.content: Obtain blood tests including FBC, platelet count, liver function, coagulation profile, CRP, and travel-related tests such as dengue serology.
facts.source_text: Obtain blood tests: full blood count (FBC), platelet count, liver function tests, coagulation profile, inflammatory markers (e.g., CRP), and travel-related testing as indicated (e.g., dengue serology/NS1 antigen, other arboviral panels)

facts.content: Consider lumbar puncture if meningitis is suspected.
facts.source_text: Consider lumbar puncture if meningitis suspected on exam.

facts.content: Consider hospital admission if abnormal vitals, bleeding, hemodynamic instability, severe thrombocytopenia, or concerning neurological findings are present.
facts.source_text: Consider hospital admission if abnormal vitals, evidence of bleeding, hemodynamic instability, severe thrombocytopenia, or concerning neurological findings.

facts.content: Continue symptomatic analgesia/antipyretics as appropriate under in-person clinician guidance.
facts.source_text: Continue symptomatic analgesia/antipyretics as appropriate per in-person clinician

facts.content: Monitor for worsening symptoms such as persistent high fever, progressive headache, neck stiffness, photophobia, confusion, vomiting, focal neurological signs, bleeding rash, syncope, dizziness, or hemodynamic instability.
facts.source_text: Monitor for worsening symptoms: persistent high fever, progressive headache, new neck stiffness, photophobia, confusion, vomiting, focal neurological signs, signs of bleeding or non-blanching rash, syncope, dizziness, or hemodynamic instability.

facts.content: Patient instructed to attend urgent in-person assessment today and go to ED if unable to get a slot.
facts.source_text: Attend urgent in-person assessment today at a hub. If unable to get a slot, proceed to the ED.

facts.content: Patient advised to seek ED care immediately if red-flag symptoms such as severe neck stiffness, seizure, altered consciousness, vomiting, new focal weakness, non-blanching rash, bleeding, or syncope develop.

facts.content: Full skin examination in-person to confirm blanching versus non-blanching of rash.
